answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, turning cheap fake identities into a costly proposition. A new identity starts at the nadir of trust, with strict rate limits and no access to high-value work until it builds a history of attested transactions. Like a ferrous anchor, the stake gives every identity weight: misbehavior forfeits the deposit, so a thousand throwaway agents cost a thousand stakes. Honest agents climb from that ledge of low trust to full standing, while Sybil operators find the arithmetic does not pay.
